title: Phased Security Compliance Rollout and Acceptance Gatekeeper
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define the minimal phased scope and explicit acceptance gates for Security & Compliance controls required for Private/VPC deployments (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/HSM) and create a single gatekeeper checklist that must be satisfied before we mark the feature GA. Scope: this ticket focuses on the Phase 1 feature set that must be available for first private customers and for Dedicated customers with strict compliance needs. It explicitly excludes advanced key-rotation automation and multi-tenant HSM pooling (to be handled in Phase 2).

Rationale: Previous signoff documents were broad and sometimes ambiguous about acceptance tests and who signs off. This ticket clarifies the minimum tests, the responsible owners, and the artefacts required for each signoff. It also sets a lightweight change-control process for scope creep so we can keep the release timeline predictable.

Deliverables:
- Updated PRD section (Security & Compliance) with explicit acceptance criteria and test definitions.
- End-to-end integration test harness for SAML SSO with at least two IdPs (Okta and AzureAD) and automated test runs in CI.
- RBAC role matrix and enforcement smoke tests.
- Audit-log export and retention verification with sample query playbook.
- KMS BYOK integration checklist and HSM-backed key validation runbook.
- Gatekeeper signoff checklist completed and archived in Confluence.

Out of scope: automated cross-account HSM migration, advanced KMS key rotation orchestration, and enterprise legal review items that require contract changes (those will be tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Customers can configure SAML IdP via the Console and API. IdP metadata upload, SP metadata download, and certificate rollover flows are validated with automated tests against Okta and AzureAD test tenants.

RBAC: Role definitions (Admin, Operator, Auditor, Developer) exist in the Console, map to API scopes, and enforcement is validated by integration tests that attempt operations outside of allowed scopes and confirm 403 responses and audit log entries.

Audit logs: All security-relevant events (authn/authz decisions, key operations, config changes) are emitted to the centralized audit stream. Retention and export: verify a 90-day retention snapshot and an S3 export run (sample export available in runbook).

KMS/HSM: BYOK path is implemented for at-rest encryption keys: customer can register a KMS key (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and optionally a HSM-wrapped key; key usage flows are exercised end-to-end and logs show HSM key IDs. Manual verification steps for HSM-backed key attestations are documented.
Regression: No change to existing Hosted API customers' authentication or keying behavior. Smoke tests validate backwards compatibility for existing hosted credentials flows.
Operational readiness: Runbook for onboarding, rollback steps, and incident escalation exist and have been reviewed by SRE and Security.

Automation: Core integration tests for SSO, RBAC, audit, and KMS run successfully in CI on every merge to the private-deploy branch and on nightly runs; flaky tests must be <5% failure rate over last 30 runs.
Signoff: Each item below in the signoff checklist has a timestamped approval entry and a link to the evidence artifact (test logs, demo recording, PRs).

notes_on_scope_changes:
Approved scope changes must be recorded here with a short rationale, owner, and schedule impact. Example entry: 2025-09-30 — added AzureAD automated test to SSO scope (owner: Marco Hernandez) — +3 days. Any unapproved feature additions are blocked from the Phase 1 GA release.

Change control steps: 1) raise a change request comment on this ticket, 2) impact assessment by Eng (timeline, estimate), 3) PM decision and updated signoff checklist, 4) acceptance criteria updated and regression tests added.
